rationale: Evidence from the last race (iteration 1, ki 0.4, kp 2.5, kd 0.2, base_speed 1.4). No run finished on any track, and all 60 trials ended off track. Progress improved modestly against the baseline: oval 0.105 to 0.168, s-bend 0.148 to 0.172, slalom 0.105 to 0.113. max_error still sits at about 0.061 on every track, which is the 0.06 m off-track limit. rms_error fell slightly (oval 0.028 to 0.022). Line_loss_events remain at 1 per run. steering_oscillation rose on oval (0.075 to 0.104) but stayed under 0.15 on all tracks, so there is no jitter sign. The integral term helped a little, which is consistent with a steady offset, but it did not remove it. The evaluator's feedback sets the next step: if progress stays near 0.1 to 0.2 with a constant-sign drift and max_error near 0.06, raise ki to about 1.0 and keep kp at 2.5. Oscillation is below the 0.15 threshold, so kp stays where it is. The integral is still clamped at +/-2 (a maximum contribution of 2 to turn at ki 1.0), which limits windup. I am changing only ki (0.4 to 1.0) so the result isolates the integral hypothesis. base_speed stays at 1.4 and kd at 0.2, because no run has finished yet, so there is no completion_time evidence to justify a speed change. Geometry is unchanged. Expected result: a larger share of the course covered before the off-track limit (progress above about 0.3), with max_error below 0.06 on at least some seeds and fewer early departures. The main risk is that a higher ki causes slow overshoot, which would show as a rise in steering_oscillation or a sign-alternating error. Next race I want per-track progress, max_error, rms_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation and completion_time. If progress is still stuck near 0.17 with a constant-sign error, the offset is not the main cause, and I would look at sensor placement or the line-loss behaviour instead. If the robot finishes, completion_time decides whether base_speed should go back toward 1.5.
